We had found it best to purchase secondhand buses in the south, as generally they were in better condition than those purchased in the north, where the harsh winters and salted roads caused their quick deterioration. Besides, Florida's ideal climate afforded our construction and engine repair crew the facility of working outdoors year-round.

Up to Seattle, Washington, we raced to catch the students before final exams and summer recess, then down to Portland for three weeks of fruitful preaching which yielded three new *bhaktas*-Robert, Bill, and Dave. Gradually we worked our way down through Oregon and at last arrived in San Francisco with six new men.

Our program was Berkeley by day, San Francisco by night. We performed our daily festivals, this time without incident, at the Berkeley campus, while returning by late afternoon to San Francisco's Mission district, where the temple was now located. Robert, the serious, mature devotee who had joined in Portland, offered his old Volkswagen minibus to serve as my traveling office. It was a welcome suggestion coming after one year of living with no privacy in the bus, squeezed together sometimes with as many as thirty *brahmacārīs*. With some slight modifications the old vehicle was transformed into a mobile *bhajana-kuṭira*, to be towed behind Rādhā-Dāmodara's bus. Recognizing Robert's level-headedness, I immediately sent him to Tampa, where his electrical ability and concern for detail would be a great asset both to the construction crew as well as in assisting Keśava Bhāratī with administration.

The annual pilgrimage to India traditionally took its toll upon American *saṅkīrtana*. Protracted cases of dysentery, exhaustion, and cultural reacclimatization sometimes cost temples months before *saṅkīrtana* fully recovered. In that sense we were fortunate to have not brought our men to India, considering them too spiritually immature to appreciate the visit fully. As a result, our *saṅkīrtana* activities continued to increase without impediment, and by May we had distributed 150,000 *Back to Godheads*, one and a half times the number of books of our closest competitor, the BBT party, and twice that of any other.

BBT party leader Tripurāri Swami now had cause for great anxiety. The freshmen book distributors of the Rādhā-Dāmodara party were serious competition, a force to be reckoned with. He moved quickly from airport to airport, urging his saṅkīrtana heroes to defeat the new challengers. Although they were only a small group, the BBT party had enjoyed unrivaled success, and in the spirit of competition they had even underreported their results, just to encourage other temples to increase their book distribution. But now Tripurāri Swami saw a party that needed no artificial inducement. The Rādhā-Dāmodara men were as fired up about *saṅkīrtana* as his, and there were a lot more of them.

When he arrived in San Francisco, Tripurāri Mahārāja found Viṣṇujana Mahārāja and I busy at our normal occupation of making new devotees. But in addition, there were two maxi-vans full of new *bhaktas* distributing thousands of *BTG's* in the Bay Area. Like chivalrous warriors after a day's fighting, we met together in the evening in warm friendship to appreciate each other's *saṅkīrtana* exploits. I prodded Tripurāri to give up his miserly ways and share some of his senior men with us. But he would have nothing to do with such an idea. Rather, he protested that it was we who were in a better position to give in charity. Outnumbered by nearly ten to one, how could he possibly compete? Though he had all of the airports, there was no facility there for making new men. Therefore, Tripurāri revealed, he had decided to get a bus of his own and start recruiting men, just as we were doing. Then he could train them up to distribute magazines in the parking lots and, for those who showed special aptitude, graduate them to positions in the airports.

I was amazed at Tripurāri Mahārāja's determination. While training and guiding not only his own distributors but those from the temples as well, he was personally distributing more books than any other man in the country. And yet now he proposed that somehow he would also run a traveling festival program. One had to be impressed. Śrīla Prabhupāda had in no way exaggerated when he had described Tripurāri Mahārāja as "the incarnation of book distribution." Just by staying with him for a few days I felt my dedication to saṅkīrtana considerably deepen.

The competition was on! There was little doubt that Tripurāri was determined to unseat us from the top position we had occupied since February. Somehow we would have to increase our book distribution significantly to stay ahead of his party. I spoke to Ādi-keśava and Dhṛṣṭadyumna by phone. Both confirmed that it was indeed possible, providing we made some basic changes. Undoubtedly our concern for book distribution was increasing, but it still played a secondary role to our festival programs. Often our *saṅkīrtana* vans were forced to remain in thinly populated areas around a university where the bus party was holding a festival. If we changed our strategy and allowed the *saṅkīrtana* vans to travel freely, concentrating wherever they found the best field for book distribution, then the results could be substantially increased. This would, however, mean that the men would not be able to return to the bus every evening, as they were still in the habit of doing. They would have to hold their own morning program at some campground or motel and perhaps return to the bus only once a week for association and encouragement as well as stocking up with more books.

To make the plan successful required expert coordination by our head office staff. The van parties would have to inform Tampa every evening of their location and leave a contact phone number for the bus leaders to reach them at. In this way, although they might only touch base with their bus once a week, they would still be able to give daily reports of the book distribution, the consciousness of each of the men, and possible new places to travel to. Keśava Bhāratī, from his position at the head office, could also preach to the individual *saṅkīrtana* van leaders, and if necessary to the men under them as well. Between speaking with Keśava Bhāratī and their bus leader, the men with the *saṅkīrtana* vans could remain nearly as enlivened as they would had they come back every evening to the bus. In fact, if this arrangement increased the number of books distributed, then the sheer potency of propagating *saṅkīrtana* would in itself be the most purifying and enlivening factor of all.

Now the importance of book distribution could run parallel to that of our festival programs. Allowing the *saṅkīrtana* vans to roam freely was like severing the umbilical cord of a newborn infant. The baby was now free to breathe on its own and very quickly began to grow by leaps and bounds. Weekly I phoned Rāmeśvara, informing him of our distribution results, while trying to pry from him information of Tripurāri Mahārāja's activities. The competition was very close, Rāmeśvara indicated, and even by the third week of June it was hard to tell who would come out ahead.

While book distribution steadily increased, the influx of new devotees attracted by our festivals also grew proportionately. Old devotees joined us as well. Ādi-keśava's bus circled the New York-Boston area, and men who had formerly served under him found the life of traveling and preaching impossible to resist. Other expert preachers, such as Jayānanda, Kavicandra, Danavīrā, and Brahmā, saw our traveling bus and van program as an ideal opportunity to facilitate their own preaching as well as their spiritual advancement. The Rādhā-Dāmodara party, based on renunciation and preaching, was an alluring format for those so inclined.

Amid such healthy *saṅkīrtana* rivalry Śrīla Prabhupāda returned to America on his second world tour in less than six months. In his opening address, shortly after arriving in Los Angeles, Śrīla Prabhupāda acclaimed, "I have no personal qualification, but I simply try to satisfy my *guru*, that's all. My Guru Mahārāja asked me, 'If you get some money, you print books.' Therefore I am stressing on this point-Where is book? Where is book? So kindly help me. That is my request. Print as many books as possible in as many languages as possible, and distribute throughout the whole world. Then the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement will automatically increase."

With leaders like Kīrtanānanda Swami, Brahmānanda Swami, Viṣṇujana Swami, Tripurāri Swami, Rāmeśvara Prabhu, and an entire temple full of dedicated preachers seated before him, Śrīla Prabhupāda sent his words like arrows of love deep into the core of every disciple's heart: "Distribute books, distribute books, print and distribute books." The message reverberated again and again. This, more than anything else, would please Śrīla Prabhupāda, for it was directly the order of his Guru Mahārāja.

In a conversation held later on in the privacy of his quarters, Śrīla Prabhupāda elaborated further. When I described that we were selling more than one hundred thousand *Back to Godheads* monthly, he inquired, "What about big books? How many are you selling?" Śrīla Prabhupāda then explained the importance of distributing his hardbound books-the *Bhagavad-gītā* and *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*. While *Back to Godhead* would give an introductory idea of our philosophy, because of its magazine format it could not compare either in comprehensiveness or durability with his big books. We should not only distribute *Back to Godhead* but all of his other books as well, especially the *Gītā* and *Bhāgavatam*.

I listened with rapt attention to Śrīla Prabhupāda's instruction. This was the first guidance I had received in person from him on the subject of distributing his books. I took it that he now considered this my foremost service to him, and he was counseling me on exactly how he wanted it done. Up to this time, nearly all the hardbound books had been distributed in the airports, where the larger donations made it feasible. But how would this be possible in a situation such as ours, where we received only small donations of often less than one dollar? This would not even cover the cost of printing the book, what to speak of any other expenses. However, I did not express my thoughts. I needed time to deeply meditate on how to execute Śrīla Prabhupāda's instruction. If this was his order, I had no doubt it could be fulfilled.

From Los Angeles Prabhupāda traveled to Denver, Colorado, along with many sannyāsīs, including Bhavānanda Goswami and Sudāmā Goswami. Seeing the success that I had had after leaving India, both Bhavānanda Mahārāja and Gargamuni Mahārāja had also decided to travel West, and each had formed his own traveling party to collect funds on behalf of Māyāpur Chandrodaya Mandira. With Rādhā-Dāmodara to care for, Viṣṇujana and I left Los Angeles a day early to be in Denver in time to greet Śrīla Prabhupāda. After a peaceful stay of four days, Śrīla Prabhupāda made preparations for the next stop on his North American tour-Chicago.

The overnight journey to Chicago seemed to span seven years of my spiritual life, rather than the twenty hours the bus actually required to cover the distance. Accompanying me were Bhavānanda Goswami and Sudāmā Mahārāja, two of my oldest Godbrothers who had been with me in the first years of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Bhavānanda and I had shared intimate service together in India, while Sudāmā had been preaching in Japan. Now once again Kṛṣṇa had brought us together in America after many years of separation. With *kīrtana* and fresh *prasādam* conveniently available aboard the bus, we spent much of the journey reminiscing about the past. But there was also talk of the future.

The forthcoming week would be a memorable one for our Rādhā-Dāmodara party. Our entire party, including the two buses just completed, would be gathering together for the first time because of Śrīla Prabhupāda's presence and the celebration of Ratha-yātrā. But for most of our young men, the most significant part of the week-long festivities would be their official acceptance into our Gauḍīya-*sampradāya* by sacred initiation received from Śrīla Prabhupāda. Many had been waiting more than a year, while others only a few months. The initiation day would mark a coming of age not only for the men individually but for our party as a whole. The image of two *sannyāsīs* with their troop of green recruits would be put to rest, and an assembly of qualified Vaiṣṇava preachers, transformed by the sacred rite of initiation would emerge. After the initiations Śrīla Prabhupāda would preside at the multiple installation of Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda Deities in each bus. By his divine grace the entire Rādhā-Dāmodara party-the Deities, devotees, vehicles, and paraphernalia-would be fully consecrated to fulfill Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mission.

\* \* \*

"Drive to the rear of the temple," I directed our new driver, Vṛkasaṅga. "I want to see our new buses." We passed down the narrow lane leading to the small parking area at the rear of our Chicago temple in the suburb of Evanston. Four Greyhound buses came into view, all bearing the identical color scheme and design of Rādhā-Dāmodara's original bus. Across the front, where normally the city's destination is shown, HARE KRISHNA was boldly displayed instead. Looking through the windows I noted that two of the buses were filled to the ceiling with cartons of books.

"Whose bus is that?" I asked Keśava Bhāratī, who had just stepped out of the temple to greet me. Toward the end of the lot was parked a long, blue-colored school bus.

"It's Tripurāri Swami's. He's just purchased it from the Toronto temple. He's gotten Parivrājakācārya Swami to join him, and they already have Gaura-Nitāi Deities for traveling. They're preaching to the same new men we wanted to introduce to you and Viṣṇujana Mahārāja," complained Keśava Bhāratī. "I've never seen Tripurāri Mahārāja this competitive."

I was not surprised. Thanks to our new *saṅkīrtana* strategy, our book distributors had been able to improve their scores. As a result we had distributed two hundred thousand *Back to Godheads* in June, just barely enough to again defeat the BBT party. Tripurāri was wasting no more time. True to Keśava Bhāratī's word, we found him in the *sannyāsī* quarters, pressing two new men to join him. The temple authorities, who had designated a large room as the *sannyāsīs'* residence for the duration of the festival, had not known that a fierce competition was building up between the two parties. It would be interesting to see how we would coexist, confined to the same quarters.

It soon became clear that a change was in order. With Tripurāri and his new companion Parivrājakācārya on one side, and Viṣṇujana, myself, and our assistants on the other, it felt more like being on the 38th parallel in Korea than the warmth of *sannyāsa* companionship. I had enjoyed the competition thus far. It had stimulated us to increase *saṅkīrtana*. Śrīla Prabhupāda had always encouraged the preachers to challenge their saṅkīrtana abilities, but up till now it had always been a friendly rivalry, with Kṛṣṇa as the ultimate benefactor. The present situation, however, seemed overly aggressive. The hushed conversations, suspicious glances, and generally secretive mood seemed to me to be antagonistic to the principle of *sādhu-saṅga*, saintly association. I liked to compete, but not under these circumstances.

Finally I confronted Tripurāri Mahārāja directly. Our friendship had only recently begun, but now I felt that we were quickly becoming adversaries. To feel estranged from the temple presidents was difficult enough, but I had never experienced such alienation among my *sannyāsī* Godbrothers. Perhaps having just taken *sannyāsa* he was yet unaware of the warm camaraderie that had always existed amongst the *sannyāsīs* in India. If we were to coexist in America, it could only be in that spirit; otherwise I wanted to have nothing to do with it.

Tripurāri Mahārāja agreed that he valued Viṣṇujana's and my friendship and certainly did not want anything to injure it. But ever since becoming a book distributor he had always been competing. It motivated him to be more determined in his service to his spiritual master, and the same was also true of the other men in his party. By being aggressive for Kṛṣṇa he had attracted Śrīla Prabhupāda's attention, and after taking *sannyāsa* he had not thought to change his mood.

But I was obstinate. He could be as aggressive as he liked-but not against me. The same new men that we would have preached to, he was now canvassing. How was Kṛṣṇa benefiting? Getting his own bus and trying to duplicate our program would only serve to distract him from his real purpose of book distribution, as managing a festival party was a full-time service. How was he planning to do both?

Tripurāri Mahārāja admitted that it would not be easy, but he was determined to make it work somehow. Prabhupāda had told him to increase book distribution, but the temples were always unwilling to supply him new men. Now he would no longer have to beg from them. "Tripurāri, why don't we join parties?" The idea was obvious. With his experienced airport distributors to train the best of our new men, a whole new group of book distributors could be created. Why should he imitate what we were already doing successfully when by combining our parties he would enjoy even more benefit than by attempting the program on his own? The combination of our two parties would usher in a whole new era of *saṅkīrtana* by developing an organized program for systematically moving the men from the position of new *bhaktas* to expert *saṅkīrtana* distributors.

Tripurāri was a little hesitant. He had just gotten the new bus and had not even had the chance to try it out. His slow deliberation exasperated me. "Tripurāri, I'm sorry, but I can't take this anymore. If you don't join me then I'm just going to send our collections to the India projects, and you can send your money to the Book Fund. But no more fighting!"

Tripurāri Mahārāja was shocked. His life was dedicated to encouraging book distribution, and now to see the party that was most enthusiastic for saṅkīrtana give up contributing to Prabhupāda's Book Fund altogether was too much for him to take. "All right! I'm ready to join you."

As news of the transcendental merger filtered down to the ranks, men of both parties applauded the "marriage" as an invincible combination. In a heady, boisterous mood, leaders from both sides went arm in arm to Prabhupāda's apartment to seek His Divine Grace's blessings. First to meet us at the door was Brahmānanda Swami, who was serving as Śrīla Prabhupāda's secretary. By now we had calmed down, and when Brahmānanda heard the purpose of our visit, he immediately let us in and arranged an interview. Within moments we were ushered into Śrīla Prabhupāda's room: Tripurāri Swami, Parivrājakācārya Swami, Viṣṇujana Swami, and myself, along with Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Ādi-keśava, Keśava Bhāratī, Kavicandra, Yogeśacandra, and Janārdana, as well as Gaṇapati and other leaders of Tripurāri's party. Prabhupāda sat like an effulgent sun amid a dozen brightly reflecting moons. These were Prabhupāda's frontline soldiers, tried and tested by many *saṅkīrtana* campaigns. He was glad that they had come to see him. As I explained how by joining forces our two parties would be able to increase the *saṅkīrtana* movement, Śrīla Prabhupāda nodded his head, indicating his approval. He liked this mood of cooperation. But we wondered what the name of our party should be-Rādhā-Dāmodara or BBT?

"Keep the name of the Rādhā-Dāmodara party," was Prabhupāda's decision.

Then I showed Śrīla Prabhupāda how we had been maintaining accurate accounting records. Keśava Bhāratī lifted the hefty accounts onto Prabhupāda's desk, and I pointed out the system of bookkeeping that Prabhupāda had originally taught me when I first traveled with him in India.

"Transcendental accounting," pronounced Śrīla Prabhupāda after giving a cursory perusal of our elaborate bookkeeping system. He was pleased to know that so much care was being taken to keep Kṛṣṇa's records in order. "Make America Kṛṣṇa conscious by distributing millions of books. That will be a blessing upon the American people and the perfection of your lives. All glories to the Rādhā-Dāmodara party!"

Śrīla Prabhupāda's BBT secretary, Rāmeśvara, was cautious in giving his approval. Hearing of the merger by telephone he expressed his concern over whether it would actually increase book distribution. In the midst of a special publishing marathon, in which Prabhupāda had ordered an unprecedented seventeen volumes of books to be printed within a two-month period, Rāmeśvara knew only too well that Śrīla Prabhupāda's satisfaction depended upon results. And Śrīla Prabhupāda relied heavily upon Rāmeśvara to insure that book distribution was always increasing. Through his BBT newsletter editorials and constant preaching over the telephone, Rāmeśvara's voice faithfully reflected Prabhupāda's concern for book distribution above all other programs.

As ISKCON was Prabhupāda's body, the BBT was his heart, and as Śrīla Prabhupāda's transcendental physician, Rāmeśvara was ever-attentive, keeping his finger on the ISKCON pulse, insuring that its heart, the BBT, was always beating strongly. Joining the two parties would eliminate the fire of competition which for months Rāmeśvara had been carefully fanning. The strength of the new Rādhā-Dāmodara party would be so overwhelming that no temple could ever hope to compete. Only when Tripurāri and I pledged that our combined distribution would surpass whatever we had done individually did Rāmeśvara become satisfied. But he would be watching carefully to see that we kept our word.

For chief administrator Keśava Bhāratī, combining the two parties was like mixing apples and oranges. While everyone else celebrated, he sat alone in the bus, reorganizing the parties, with cases of Prabhupāda's books stacked to the ceiling as his only company. Keeping track of 125 men, 6 buses, and 20 vans, all moving in different directions throughout America, was impossible for a mere one-headed, two-armed human being, he concluded.

\* \* \*

**July 10, 1975**

In the high-ceilinged black-and-white-tiled temple room, seventy-five *brahmacārīs* sat awaiting initiation. The vast room no longer bore any trace of its former gymnasium appearance. Instead, at one end were three arched doors now opened to reveal the *arcā-vigraha* forms of Lord Caitanya and Nityānanda, Śrī Śrī Kiśora-Kiśorī, and Lord Jagannātha, Balarāma, and Subhadra. Present especially to witness the function being held in Their honor were Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Dāmodara. (Moments earlier, four eighteen-inch pairs of Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda Deities had been bathed and dressed and carried ceremoniously to each bus for installation.) At the opposite end of the temple room, between its two entrances, Śrīla Prabhupāda sat, facing the Deities, ready to preside over the largest initiation ceremony ever held in ISKCON. Prabhupāda had chosen the day before his Chicago departure to hold the Deity installation and initiation ceremony. With the cooperation of the local devotees, the temple room was nicely decorated with auspicious markings, flags, banners, and festoons. It was an unusual event considering it was being conducted solely for devotees not residing at that temple.

I handed Śrīla Prabhupāda the list of names he had approved, selected mainly from the associates of Lord Caitanya. The whole room was pregnant with silence as all awaited to hear each of the devotees' new spiritual names. The sound of Śrīla Prabhupāda clearing his voice came over the loudspeaker system. I instructed the devotees to line up in single file. After receiving their initiation beads, they were to offer full obeisances before their spiritual master. They began to come forward. Śrīla Prabhupāda handed Gordon his beads. "Your name is Gaurāṅga dāsa." Tom was next. "Your name is Śrī Rāma dāsa." Then Tracy: "Śrīkara dāsa." Chris: "Sañjaya dāsa." Elton: "Sarvopama dāsa." Robert: "Rājendranātha dāsa." "Gopāla Ācārya dāsa Govinda Datta dāsa Yadugaṅguli dāsa Choṭahari dāsa Ācāryaratna dāsa Caitanyacandra dāsa Karṇapūra dāsa Dhṛṣṭa dāsa . . ."

The weekly Saṅkīrtana Newsletter reported the news of the Chicago events to the ISKCON world:

"The leaders of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Dāmodara TSKP and BBT TSKP, with the blessings of Śrīla Prabhupāda, met together in Chicago during the Ratha-yātrā festival; the details of that meeting are being enclosed herein. With Viṣṇujana Swami as the inspiration; Tamal Krishna Goswami as the cohesive organizing force; Tripurāri Mahārāja providing the sincere zeal for *saṅkīrtana*, Sudāmā Mahārāja's stimulating love and devotion for the four new sets of Gaura-Nitāi Deities installed simultaneously by Śrīla Prabhupāda; and Parivrājakācārya Mahārāja inspiring scholarly assimilation of Śrīla Prabhupāda's books, the following saṅkīrtana parties were sent out in ecstasy.

There are six festival buses, headed by Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Dāmodara and Their attendants Viṣṇujana Swami and Tamal Krishna Goswami. Sudāmā Mahārāja and soon-to-be *sannyāsī* Dhṛṣṭadyumna dāsa *Brahmacārī* head a bus called Nimāi-Nitāi. Śrīmān Ādi-keśava dāsa heads a bus of potent preachers and distributors. Parivrājakācārya Mahārāja and Danavīra dāsa make a potent combination for making new devotees. And two former BBT big-book distributors, Kavicandra dāsa and Brahmā dāsa, have each taken leadership of a new bus for Their Lordships Gaura-Nitāi.

"Each of these parties puts on *saṅkīrtana* festivals in every town and village, chanting, dancing, distributing *bhagavat-prasādam*, preaching, and spreading the glories of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Soon each bus will begin a tour of major college campuses and will pick up new *brahmacārīs* to fill the new buses that are being constructed by a party of devotees in their Tampa, Florida, head office. Each festival bus also provides shelter and direction for satellite maxi-vans and cars filled with enthusiastic book distributors who go out on half- and full-day parties assisting Śrīla Prabhupāda in spreading the glories of the Lord.

"Then there are the hard-core distributors, led by Yogeśacandra dāsa, Janārdana dāsa, Pyāri-Mohana dāsa, Prahlādānanda dāsa, and Gaṇapati dāsa, each of whom is sent out in five maxi-vans in parties of four men each to scour every nook and cranny of every town and village, distributing Śrīla Prabhupāda's books in parking lots, fairs, and malls. Anywhere and everywhere conditioned souls congregate, they find bright-faced Rādhā-Dāmodara *brahmacārīs* to lift them out of their material bodies to associate with the pure devotee through his transcendental sound vibrations: BTGs, Kṛṣṇa books, *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*-the greatest benediction to the educated minds of the Western world.

"And for the souls who escape this network of mercy woven by Rādhā-Dāmodara festival buses and traveling vans, there are the airports, with the most experienced and talented big-book distributors, trained by Tripurāri Mahārāja and led by Praghoṣa dāsa, Sura dāsa, and Naikātmā dāsa, distributing big books to scientists, philosophers, educators, politicians, businessmen, students, and servicemen in Chicago, Atlanta, San Francisco, Philadelphia, and Denver. These great personalities must adapt their preaching to all types of conditioned souls and are distributing phenomenal numbers of Prabhupāda's big books. These experienced preachers look forward to new frontiers as Rādhā-Dāmodara opens new airports in August to accommodate the seven extra airport distributors coming from the Rādhā-Dāmodara bus parties.

"These seventeen parties form a tightly run organization where the results of their preaching and book distribution are known by and accounted for: each book, each piece of incense, each penny collected-practically as fast as they are distributed. Every month the totals are projected in advance amazingly close to the actual result by the grace of Śrīla Prabhupāda's managing methods."

The roster of men and their specific assignments revealed the amazing growth of our party.
